events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
The rider disputes a $6.61 no-show cancellation fee after the driver cancelled at 12:09:05, claiming the driver marked arrived but was never at the pickup point [F3][F7]. NS-0 routes this to the NS-1/NS-2 branch because cancellation was by the driver on a no-show claim [F3][RD-1]... applying NS-0: cancelled_by = driver and driver asserts rider no-show, so NS-1/NS-2 govern.

NS-1 requires all three of (i) "I'm Here" pressed, (ii) GPS position at the pickup point at the time of the tap, and (iii) more than 3 minutes waited within the pickup radius. Element (i) is satisfied — the trace shows a tap at 12:05:55 [F5] — and the driver's chat and statement assert he pressed it and waited [F9][F11][F12]. However element (ii) fails: at the moment of the tap the driver was 601 m from the pickup point, and his closest approach for the whole trip was 545 m, so he never entered the 200 m arrival radius [F5][F1][NS-1]. The platform also never recorded an arrival (driver_arrived_at is null) [F4][NS-1]. Element (iii) also fails: he stayed 0 s continuously inside the radius after the tap [F5], and his 3 min 30 s stationary period at 600 m from the pickup [F2] was spent outside the pickup area, so it does not count as waiting at the pickup [NS-1]. With (ii) and (iii) unmet, the $6.61 fee cannot stand.

Because NS-1's conditions are not all met, NS-2 applies directly: the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider [F7][NS-2]. System records (gps and timeline: 545 m closest approach, 601 m at the tap, no recorded arrival) outweigh the driver's statements that he was at the pickup and waited [F1][F4][F5][F12][NS-2].

Separately, NS-2's second limb is triggered: the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS shows he was not at the pickup point (tap at 601 m, [F5]; closest approach 545 m, [F1]), which is an abuse of the arrival/waiting button and requires an account flag [NS-2]. The rider's own no-show history is clean (0 disputes, 0 upheld) [F16], and the driver's clean 90-day record [F17] does not cure the false arrival tap; profile facts cannot decide the case either way [NS-2].

Amount: the disputed fee is the cancellation fee of $6.61 [F7][F3]; no other charge is in dispute, so the refund equals $6.61 [NS-2].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We've reviewed your dispute of the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee and are refunding it in full. GPS records show the driver was about 600 metres from the pickup point when he tapped "I'm Here", and never got closer than roughly 545 metres, so he never reached the pickup area and the arrival wasn't recorded. The fee can't stand. The $6.61 comes to you as a Ryde voucher, applied automatically to your account. Nothing else is needed from you.

DRIVER: We reviewed a no-show cancellation on your account. The GPS record shows you tapped "I'm Here" while about 600 metres from the pickup point, and your closest approach was roughly 545 metres, so you never entered the pickup area. Because of that we've refunded the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher, and your account is going to Ryde review over the arrival tap. A reviewer will look at your arrival tap and location records for that trip. No action is needed from you right now.
